classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied enclosing rectangles and subdivisions to recognise half-rectangle triangles, then combine two or four such areas algebraically.

content.prompt: Find the area of each of these shapes in terms of $x$ and $y$.

spec.description: Right triangle and its attached enclosing rectangle. Light blue identifies the requested region; red dashed lines retain the enclosing-area scaffold.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular sides x cm and y cm; the triangle occupies half of its enclosing rectangle.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and construction only; no area answer.

answer.worked:
The triangle is half of the enclosing rectangle, whose area is $xy\ \mathrm{cm}^2$.

$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{x\times y}{2}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$

spec.description: Triangle with an internal perpendicular altitude, two labelled base segments and attached dashed enclosing rectangle.
spec.mathematics: Altitude x cm; each half-base y cm. Each of the two right triangles is half of an x by y rectangle.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied lengths and right-angle mark visible; no area answer.

answer.worked:
Each of the two right triangles is half of a rectangle with sides $x$ cm and $y$ cm.

$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{xy}{2}+\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=xy\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$

spec.description: Diamond-shaped quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals, all four half-diagonal labels and an enclosing dashed rectangle.
spec.mathematics: Four right triangles, each with perpendicular sides x cm and y cm; enclosing rectangle dimensions 2x cm by 2y cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied subdivisions and labels visible; no area answer.

answer.worked:
The diagonals divide the shape into four right triangles. Each is half of an $x$ cm by $y$ cm rectangle.

$\begin{align*}A&=4\times\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=2xy\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$
